We say that a vertex v € V(G)| D is D-defended if there exists a vertex u € N(v)nD such that (D {u}) U {v} is a dominating set of G. Specifically; we say that v € V(G) D is Ddefended by a vertex u if u € N(v)nD and (D {u})U {v} is a dominating set of G. We note that D is a secure dominating set of G if and only if every vertex in V(G) D is D-defended.
